title: --cpu (and likely --amd) engine installs pull the whole CUDA stack: --fast-deps ignores the vendor flag
description: Found 2026-07-30 on the Linux desktop during MPI-391 section D, on a GPU-less ThinkPad. _provisionUvEngine builds installArgs at routes/engine.js:373-375 and passes --fast-deps for every vendor except --m-series. comfy-cli's DependencyCompiler ignores the vendor flag and resolves generic PyPI torch, which on Linux pins the entire CUDA 13 stack. Measured from the engine's own requirements.compiled: torch==2.13.0 (bare, no +cpu tag), triton==3.7.1, nvidia-cublas, nvidia-cudnn-cu13, nvidia-cufft, nvidia-cufile, nvidia-curand, nvidia-cusolver, nvidia-cusparse, nvidia-cusparselt, nvidia-nccl-cu13, nvidia-nvjitlink, nvidia-nvshmem, nvidia-nvtx, nvidia-cuda-cupti/nvrtc/runtime. Several GB of wheels that a CPU-only box can never execute. NOT broken - CUDA torch falls back to CPU and runs - but it is a large wasted download, disk footprint and decompression load on exactly the machines least able to afford it. The same failure mode is ALREADY documented one branch over: engine.js:370-372 exempts Apple Silicon from --fast-deps for precisely this reason (no Apple-Silicon branch in DependencyCompiler, falls through to generic PyPI torch). macOS got the exemption, --cpu did not. FIX: extend the --m-series exemption to --cpu, i.e. omit --fast-deps whenever the vendor is not nvidia, so comfy-cli's standard vendor-aware install picks the CPU wheel index. SWEEP: --amd keeps --fast-deps too and is suspect for the same reason (would it resolve ROCm torch, or generic PyPI CUDA?) - verify before assuming. Windows is unaffected (prebuilt-archive path, never reaches _provisionUvEngine). NOT a 1.3.0 regression - this predates the release.
